content: In Ecclesiastes, the Teacher says to everything there is a what?
explanation: A time for every purpose under heaven. “To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven” (Ecclesiastes 3:1, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to plant and a time to do what?
explanation: Life has its seasons. “a time to plant and a time to uproot” (Ecclesiastes 3:2, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to weep and a time to do what?
explanation: Both sorrow and joy have their time. “a time to weep and a time to laugh” (Ecclesiastes 3:4, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to mourn and a time to do what?
explanation: Sadness does not last forever. “a time to mourn and a time to dance” (Ecclesiastes 3:4, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to be silent and a time to do what?
explanation: Wisdom knows when to talk. “a time to be silent and a time to speak” (Ecclesiastes 3:7, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time for war and a time for what?
explanation: Everything has its time. “a time for war and a time for peace.” (Ecclesiastes 3:8, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what has God made beautiful in its time?
explanation: He set eternity in our hearts. “He has made everything beautiful in its time.” (Ecclesiastes 3:11, BSB)

content: Who is the Teacher whose words fill Ecclesiastes?
explanation: He was king in Jerusalem. “These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem” (Ecclesiastes 1:1, BSB)

content: What does the Teacher in Ecclesiastes say everything is?
explanation: Life without God has no lasting meaning. “Everything is futile!” (Ecclesiastes 1:2, BSB)

content: According to the Teacher in Ecclesiastes, there is nothing new where?
explanation: What has been will be again. “there is nothing new under the sun.” (Ecclesiastes 1:9, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, why are two better than one?
explanation: If one falls, the other lifts him up. “For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up” (Ecclesiastes 4:10, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what kind of cord is not quickly broken?
explanation: Together we are stronger. “Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.” (Ecclesiastes 4:12, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, since God is in heaven and you are on earth, how should your words be?
explanation: Do not be quick to speak. “So let your words be few.” (Ecclesiastes 5:2, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what is never satisfied by money?
explanation: Loving wealth brings no rest. “He who loves money is never satisfied by money” (Ecclesiastes 5:10, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, when should you remember your Creator?
options: In the days of your youth
explanation: Before hard days come. “Remember your Creator in the days of your youth” (Ecclesiastes 12:1, BSB)

content: How does the Teacher sum up everything at the end of Ecclesiastes?
explanation: It is the whole duty of man. “Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.” (Ecclesiastes 12:13, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, how should you do whatever your hands find to do?
explanation: Life's time is limited. “Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might” (Ecclesiastes 9:10, BSB)

content: Over what was the Teacher of Ecclesiastes king?
explanation: He was David's son. “I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.” (Ecclesiastes 1:12, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what has God set in the hearts of men?
explanation: Yet we cannot fathom all God's work. “He has also set eternity in the hearts of men” (Ecclesiastes 3:11, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, a patient spirit is better than what?
explanation: The end is better than the beginning. “and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.” (Ecclesiastes 7:8, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, what are we told to cast upon the waters?
explanation: After many days you will find it again. “Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.” (Ecclesiastes 11:1, BSB)

content: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to cast away stones and a time to do what?
explanation: Everything has its time. “a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together” (Ecclesiastes 3:5, BSB)
